definitions.note: the sailor of the Arabian Nights tales; the 's stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay

parts.note: a fall from grace is a sin, a moral lapse
rubbish as an adjective means bad, poor quality

explanation.surface: A question about a seaman's disgrace, dismissed with a scornful 'Rubbish'.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Sailor' is 'is', a link: the question mark hints that a moral lapse and rubbish are two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary seafarer of the Thousand and One Nights is the best-known sailor in fiction.

explanation.surface: A question whether a policeman is first-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Tip-top means excellent, informal super; a super is slang for a police superintendent, a senior cop.

indicators.note: the word in tells us the saint's letters go inside the word for an obstacle

parts.note: a barrier is an obstacle or difficulty
a saint is a good man, abbreviated ST

explanation.surface: Praise for someone reliable when trouble strikes.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue also describes the courtroom lawyer you want beside you when in legal trouble, so it is its own definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtroom lawyer is just the helper you need when legal trouble arrives.

clue.text: Outrage finding counterfeit grand on time

indicators.note: in a down clue, one thing on another sits above it, so the G comes before the word for time

parts.note: a dud is a fake, such as a counterfeit coin
G is slang shorthand for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars
an eon is a vast stretch of time

explanation.surface: Indignation on discovering a fake thousand-pound note just in time.
explanation.definitionFit: Dudgeon is a feeling of offended resentment, as in 'in high dudgeon'.

clue.text: Substitutes on last of cup ties

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in a letter heading

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word cup is used

parts.note: laces are ties, as in tying shoes

explanation.surface: Swapping players before the last round of cup matches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Substitutes' and 'cup ties' suggest football, but 'ties' is laces, not matches.
explanation.definitionFit: To substitute something is to put another thing in its place.

parts.note: read not as money but as a carer who tends patients and is officially licensed to do so

explanation.surface: Asking about valid currency.
explanation.definitionFit: A qualified nurse on the official register is a lawful tender of the sick.

indicators.note: contains means one word holds the other pieces within it

parts.note: a pet is a treasured favourite, as in teacher's pet
to box is to hit, as is to rap

explanation.surface: A bank's treasure is kept in a strongbox.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' and 'treasure' suggest money; 'box' is a verb, to strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A parapet is a protective wall or raised earth embankment along a rampart or bridge.

indicators.note: after means the first word comes later than the word for a criminal

parts.note: a con is a convict, a criminal; the 's is a link
done in the sense of completed, carried out, as a duty is discharged

explanation.surface: A convicted criminal is released and then pardoned.
explanation.definitionFit: To condone is to overlook or forgive an offence.

indicators.note: returning means the abbreviation for American is read backwards
injured signals the letters of instead are damaged into a new order

explanation.surface: An American coming back with an injury got some help instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns US into SU; 'injured' rearranges INSTEAD into STAINED.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain is to support or keep going, so sustained means helped along.

parts.note: to stand something somewhere is to put it there
to clear a place of something is to rid it

explanation.surface: An instruction to stand up and clear off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clear off' looks like a phrase; the definition is 'off', meaning gone bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has gone off is rotten and stinking.

indicators.note: in means the department goes inside the word for men's

parts.note: the gents is a men's lavatory
an arm is a branch or department of an organisation

explanation.surface: A store's department selling menswear.
explanation.definitionFit: Garments are articles of clothing.

clue.text: Sir canes new form for vulgarity

indicators.note: new form says the letters of sir canes are given a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A headmaster's caning reshaped as an act of crudeness.
explanation.definitionFit: Raciness is risqué, suggestive quality, bordering on coarseness.

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father; the 's is a link
God the Father, so father can be God; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A grandfather's place of worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Father's father' suggests grandfather, but each 'father' is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagoda is a tiered Buddhist or Hindu temple, a sacred building.

clue.text: Coppers holding alien on resistance front

indicators.note: holding means the word for coppers wraps round the other letters

parts.note: copper coins are pence

indicators.note: on places the alien's letters after the resistance letter

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance
ET, the film extraterrestrial, is a crossword alien

explanation.surface: Police arresting an extraterrestrial at the front of the resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' suggests police; here it is coins, PENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A front is a false show or facade, a pretence of being something.

clue.text: Parking sign catches bird — one marvels

indicators.note: catches means the bird's letters are caught between the others

parts.note: P is the road sign abbreviation for parking
an omen is a sign or portent
a hen is a female bird
a means one, as in a dozen

explanation.surface: A traffic sign snags a bird; someone marvels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parking sign' reads as one item, but it is P plus OMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenomena are remarkable things or events, wonders.

indicators.note: in means the two single letters go inside the word for spin

parts.note: a turn is a spin or rotation
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter, E

explanation.surface: An English lover in a whirl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' is a crossword convention: the middle letter of 'sweet'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tureen is a deep serving bowl for soup.

clue.text: Driving off us peril with no resolution

indicators.note: resolution in the sense of breaking up and resolving into parts signals rearranging the letters

explanation.surface: Fending off danger to us with no firm will.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolution' is the anagram signal, applied to US PERIL plus NO.
explanation.definitionFit: Repulsion is the act of repelling or beating back an attack.

clue.text: Runs from former wife's endless nonsense

parts.note: an ex is a former wife; the 's is a link

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is cut off the word for nonsense

parts.note: trash is rubbish or nonsense

explanation.surface: An ex-wife's endless drivel causes someone to run off.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, extras are runs not scored off the bat, such as wides and byes.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket scoring counts byes, wides and no-balls as bonus runs for the batting side.

indicators.note: middle picks the central letter of the seven-letter word eastern

parts.note: bosses are studs or knobs, like rivets

explanation.surface: Backing for the bosses of the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle eastern' looks like a region; it gives the middle letter of 'eastern'.
explanation.definitionFit: A trivet is a three-legged stand supporting a pot or kettle.

indicators.note: its presence means the answer is physically there inside the words aspect reveals

explanation.surface: A frightful apparition makes itself known.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits within 'aSPECT REveals'; the whole clue also describes a ghost making itself felt.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectre is a ghost, a fearsome apparition.

indicators.note: opening means only the first letter of eye is taken

parts.note: clips are ammunition magazines for guns
ED, short for editor, is a crossword journalist; the 's means has

explanation.surface: A reporter has covered startling magazine stories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eye-opening' looks like 'surprising'; it gives just E.
explanation.definitionFit: When the moon eclipses the sun it blocks it out, hiding it from view.

indicators.note: in means the politician and energy letters go inside the word for cant

parts.note: to cant is to tilt or lean, as is to list
MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A feeble politician's vigour lost in hypocritical talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cant' suggests hypocrisy; here it means a tilt, LIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Limp means floppy and lacking strength, so the superlative is the feeblest.

parts.note: PI is a private investigator, a detective
ate means consumed food

explanation.surface: A veteran sleuth took drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: An opiate is a drug derived from opium, a narcotic.

indicators.note: travelling signals that the letters of salesman move around

parts.note: taken as written in its plural form, the only form whose letters fit the grid

explanation.surface: An unknown door-to-door salesman.
explanation.walkthrough: As held, the clue reads 'salesman', which is one letter off: the anagram works only with SALESMEN. 'travelling' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone obscure is unknown, without fame or a name to speak of.

definitions.note: to roast is to criticise harshly; the 's stands for 'is'

indicators.note: in a down clue the second word sits on top of the first, so S comes first

parts.note: late means delayed

explanation.surface: The Sunday roast is running late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roast' suggests the Sunday meal; it is the verb to criticise.
explanation.definitionFit: To slate a play is to criticise it severely.

indicators.note: manoeuvre means move the letters of a lever to into a new pattern

explanation.surface: Instructions to shift a lever.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram fodder includes 'to': A LEVER TO.
explanation.definitionFit: In American English an elevator is what the British call a lift.

clue.text: Puzzle of vague image surrounding new leader

indicators.note: surrounding means the rearranged image letters wrap round another letter
vague signals that the letters of image are blurred into a new order
leader means the first letter of new

explanation.surface: A puzzle in a blurry picture of a new chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vague' rearranges IMAGE into E-IGMA, which surrounds N.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigma is a mystery, something baffling.

indicators.note: in places the male pronoun inside the rearranged letters
refined in the sense of purified and reworked signals rearranging the letters

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
the head of egg is its first letter

explanation.surface: Is a man of cultivated tastes an intellectual?
explanation.walkthrough: 'refined' rearranges TASTE to AESTT; the whole clue then describes a person of cultivated taste, so it doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An aesthete is someone devoted to art and beauty, of cultivated sensibility.

indicators.note: leader's means the first letter of Tory

parts.note: an angle is a position or point of view

explanation.surface: Muddle about the Conservative chief's stance.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangle is a muddle, a mess.
